slides.theory_explanation: The Real Hook: Garuda Indonesia (GIAA) FY2025. Demonstrates that narrowing accounting losses (~39% YoY) can mask reliance on external capital injections (Rp 23.67T from Danantara) to avoid negative equity and delisting.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo mirrors Garuda! In 2025, GoTo's net loss narrowed from (Rp 5.47T) to (Rp 1.50T), and cash rose to Rp 21.76T. Amateurs cheered a turnaround. The reality: operating cash flow was only +Rp 307 bn vs Rp 1,182 bn Capex. Cash rose solely because GoTo liquidated Rp 1.39T of time deposits and borrowed Rp 3.72T in new bank debt, doubling total debt to Rp 7.74T.

slides.subtitle: What to Remember from Today
slides.raw_text:
K E Y  T A K E A W A Y S
What to Remember from Today
The same financial statements serve radically different users ,  always ask whose question 
you're answering.
The six-step framework separates understanding a company (Steps 1-3) from projecting it 
forward (Steps 4-6).
Wahlen gives the process; Subramanyam gives the specific tools ,  both recur all term.
Every week of this course has a specific address on the six-step map ,  this is a progression, 
not a list.
Next: a short diagnostic, group formation, and the company shortlist.
slides.theory_explanation: Key Takeaways from Week 1. 1) User determines question; 2) Steps 1-3 look back, Steps 4-6 look forward; 3) Wahlen provides process, Subramanyam provides tools; 4) Progression, not a disconnected list.
slides.goto_explanation: These principles prevent valuation errors: we never assume profitability without proving the operational mechanism, and we always tie our recommendation to the public equity investor.

slides.subtitle: Covers a PERIOD of time (e.g., the year ended Dec 31, 2025)
slides.raw_text:
1. Income Statement
Covers a PERIOD of time (e.g., the year ended Dec 31, 2025)
Shows whether the company generated a profit by matching revenues 
earned against the expenses incurred to earn them.
• Revenue ,  what was earned from customers
• Cost of Goods Sold → Gross Profit
• Operating Expenses → EBIT (Operating Income)
• Interest Expense & T ax → Net Income
• Net Income flows into the Statement of Changes in Equity
2. Statement of Changes in Equity
Covers a PERIOD of time, rolling equity forward
Shows how and why total shareholders' equity moved from the 
beginning to the end of the period.
• Beginning Equity balance
• + Net Income (from the Income Statement)
• - Dividends Paid; +/- share issuances or buybacks
• = Ending Equity balance → feeds the Balance Sheet
3. Balance Sheet (or Statement of Financial Position)
A SNAPSHOT at one point in time (e.g., as of Dec 31, 2025)
Shows what the company owns, what it owes, and what belongs to 
shareholders ,  at that single moment.
• Assets = Liabilities + Equity (always)
• Current vs. non-current assets and liabilities
• Cash balance ties to the Statement of Cash Flows
• Equity balance ties to the Statement of Changes in Equity
4. Statement of Cash Flows
Covers a PERIOD of time, reconciling cash actually received and paid
Explains why cash went up or down ,  separating operating, investing, 
and financing activity so readers can see cash quality.
• Operating (CFO) ,  cash from core business, starts from Net Income
• Investing (CFI) ,  capex, acquisitions, asset sales
• Financing (CFF) ,  debt, equity, dividends
• Ending cash ties directly to Cash on the Balance Sheet
S U M M A R Y
Anatomy of the Financial Statements
slides.theory_explanation: Period vs Point-in-Time: Income statement measures performance over 365 days; balance sheet measures financial position at midnight on December 31.

What to Remember from Today
The four statements aren't independent ,  net income and cash both trace back to the same 
balance sheet, through different paths.
Accrual accounting matches revenue with the effort that generated it ,  and is exactly why net 
income and cash flow can diverge.
The real substance of an annual report lives in the notes and the auditor's opinion, not the 
glossy front pages.
Strategy analysis comes first because you cannot judge a number without understanding the 
business behind it.

work against a company.

Week 3 Asset & Liability Valuation

slides.goto_explanation: Goodwill from the 2021 Gojek-Tokopedia merger is the textbook example of historical cost staleness. Capitalized at Rp 93.8 trillion based on peak tech-bubble valuations in May 2021, the historical cost became completely detached from reality, culminating in the 2023 mega write-off.

slides.subtitle: The 3-Step DuPont Decomposition
slides.raw_text:
TOOL 3 OF 3
The 3-Step DuPont Decomposition
ROE = Net Profit Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 5
slides.theory_explanation: The 3-step DuPont equation decomposes Return on Equity into three distinct drivers: ROE = (Net Income / Revenue) × (Revenue / Total Assets) × (Total Assets / Equity). The first term measures operational profitability, the second measures asset utilization efficiency, and the third measures financial leverage.
slides.goto_explanation: In GoTo's FY2025: Net Margin = -8.20%, Asset Turnover = 0.400x, Equity Multiplier = 1.593x. Multiplying them: -8.20% × 0.400 × 1.593 = -5.23% ROE. This mathematically accounts for every rupiah of GoTo's return.

Asset Turnover
Revenue ÷ Total Assets

Higher asset turnover indicates capital efficiency and an asset-light business model, while low turnover reflects capital intensity, idle capacity, or excessive balance sheet bloat.

slides.subtitle: Equity Multiplier (Financial Leverage)
slides.raw_text:
DRIVER 3 OF 3
Equity Multiplier
Total Assets ÷ Shareholders' Equity
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 5
slides.theory_explanation: The Equity Multiplier measures financial leverage. It reflects how many dollars of assets the company controls per dollar of shareholder equity: Equity Multiplier = Total Assets / Equity = 1 + (Total Debt / Equity). Leverage magnifies ROE: boosting positive returns in good years, but accelerating insolvency in bad years.

slides.raw_text:

Common Pitfalls
Distortions That Invalidate Ratio Analysis

slides.subtitle: Four Lenses on Risk: Liquidity, Solvency, Coverage & Distress
slides.raw_text:
THE FRAMEWORK
Four Lenses on Risk
1. Liquidity (Short-term)
2. Solvency (Long-term)
3. Coverage (Serviceability)
4. Distress Modeling (Altman Z-Score)
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 6
slides.theory_explanation: A robust financial risk assessment requires examining four complementary dimensions: (1) Liquidity evaluates immediate cash buffers over next 12 months; (2) Solvency assesses capital structure and long-term leverage; (3) Coverage tests whether current cash flow covers debt service; and (4) Distress Modeling synthesizes multivariate ratios into a single bankruptcy predictor.
slides.goto_explanation: Applying this 4-lens framework to GoTo FY2025 produces a fascinating divergence: Lens 1 (Liquidity) looks stellar; Lens 2 (Solvency) shows fast-rising debt; Lens 3 (Coverage) reveals severe cash flow inadequacy; and Lens 4 (Altman Z) predicts deep distress.

RATIO 1
Current Ratio
Current Assets ÷ Current Liabilities
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 6
slides.theory_explanation: The Current Ratio measures the margin of safety provided by short-term assets over short-term claims: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities. A ratio above 1.5x generally indicates adequate liquidity, while a ratio below 1.0x signals working capital distress.

slides.subtitle: Quick Ratio (Acid-Test): (Cash + Equivalents + Receivables) ÷ Current Liabilities
slides.raw_text:
RATIO 2
Quick Ratio (Acid-Test)
(Cash + Marketable Securities + Receivables) ÷ Current Liabilities
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 6
slides.theory_explanation: The Quick Ratio strips out illiquid current assets (such as physical inventory and prepaid expenses) to measure whether the firm can settle all short-term debts using immediately realizable liquid funds: Quick Ratio = (Cash + Marketable Securities + Receivables) / Current Liabilities. A ratio above 1.0x is considered acid-test safe.

slides.theory_explanation: Solvency evaluates a company's financial architecture and ability to meet long-term fixed obligations over a multi-year horizon. While liquidity is about cash flow timing, solvency is about capital adequacy: does the business have enough equity to absorb sustained losses without defaulting on creditors?

Debt-to-Assets Ratio & Debt-to-Equity Ratio
Measuring Capital Gearing
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 6
slides.theory_explanation: Two primary ratios govern solvency: (1) Debt-to-Assets = Total Debt / Total Assets, which indicates the fraction of total resources financed by creditors; and (2) Debt-to-Equity = Total Debt / Total Equity, which measures the financial leverage multiple borne by shareholders.

slides.subtitle: The Altman Z-Score: Multivariate Credit Distress Prediction
slides.raw_text:
LENS 4 OF 4
The Altman Z-Score
Multivariate Credit Distress Prediction
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 6
slides.theory_explanation: Developed by Edward Altman (1968, 2000), the Altman Z-score combines five weighted financial ratios into a single score that predicts bankruptcy probability with over 80-90% accuracy within a two-year horizon. It addresses the flaw of single ratios by looking at liquidity, cumulative profitability, operating efficiency, leverage, and asset turnover simultaneously.
slides.goto_explanation: Applying the 5-variable Altman Z-score to GoTo yields Z = -2.81, placing GoTo in the Distress Zone (< 1.81) due primarily to X2 (accumulated losses) and X3 (negative EBIT). Following Week 6 Slides 14-20, analysts examine all five components alongside Liquidity, Solvency, and Coverage.

Five Components, One Score

THE RESULT
Putting It Together
Original Z (-2.81) vs. Emerging Market Z'' (-11.29)

slides.theory_explanation: For emerging market and non-manufacturing / service companies, Altman developed the four-variable Z''-score model: Z'' = 6.56·X1 + 3.26·X2 + 6.72·X3 + 1.05·X4 (where X4 uses Book Value of Equity instead of Market Value, and X5 is removed to eliminate sales distortion). HANDLE WITH CARE
A Caveat Worth Paying Attention To
Negative Equity in X4 & Screening with the Four Lenses

Linking Risk Ratios to Credit Decisions
How Banks and Creditors Actually Evaluate GoTo

They establish financial covenants: contractual conditions that require the borrower to maintain minimum liquidity (Current Ratio >= 1.25x), maximum leverage (Debt / Equity <= 2.0x), and minimum cash reserves. Breaching a covenant gives the bank the right to demand immediate full loan repayment.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo's bank loan agreements (detailed in Note 17) require maintaining minimum cash balances in escrow and limits on additional indebtedness. GoTo complies with all bank covenants because its cash hoard (Rp 21.8T) comfortably exceeds all debt covenants.

slides.subtitle: Why Accounting Quality Is Distinct from Operating Performance

THE CORE IDEA
Why Accounting Quality Is a Distinct Question
Performance: How well is the business doing?
Quality: How well do the numbers reflect it?
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 7
slides.theory_explanation: Operating Performance evaluates economic success (market share, unit economics, revenue growth). Accounting Quality evaluates information integrity (conservatism, transparency, persistence of earnings). A firm can possess brilliant performance with aggressive accounting, or mediocre performance with pristine accounting.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo's operating performance is currently in a turnaround phase (loss narrowed by 98% from 2023 peak). Its accounting quality is generally solid (conservatively deducting driver subsidies under PSAK 72), with one major flag: capitalizing Rp 880.3 bn of software development.

slides.subtitle: Four Red Flags to Watch For in Financial Statements
slides.raw_text:
THE FRAMEWORK
Four Red Flags to Watch For
1. Revenue Recognition Tricks
2. One-Time Items Masking Operations
3. Related-Party Concentration
4. Inconsistent Segment Reporting
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 7
slides.theory_explanation: Forensic financial analysts monitor four classic warning signals of earnings manipulation: (1) Revenue Recognition Tricks (premature booking, gross vs. net agent games); (2) One-Time Items Masking Recurring Operations (burying recurring expenses in restructuring charges); (3) Related-Party Concentration (off-market pricing with affiliates); and (4) Inconsistent Segment Reporting (reshuffling segments to bury underperforming units).
slides.goto_explanation: Auditing GoTo across these four red flags provides a masterclass: Red Flag 1 is clean; Red Flag 2 requires normalizing the Rp 70.3T Tokopedia gain; Red Flag 3 requires tracking TikTok fees; and Red Flag 4 requires reconciling the 2024 segment reorganization.

slides.subtitle: Revenue Recognition Tricks: Principal vs. Agent under PSAK 72
slides.raw_text:
RED FLAG 1 OF 4
Revenue Recognition Tricks
Gross vs. Net Reporting & Driver Incentive Accounting
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 7
slides.theory_explanation: Under PSAK 72 (IFRS 15), if a company acts as an agent (facilitating transactions between buyers and third-party sellers), it can only recognize the net commission fee as revenue. If it acts as a principal (controlling the good or service before transfer), it can recognize gross merchandise value (GMV). Grossing up revenue inflates scale without adding a single dollar of profit.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo strictly reports on a Net Revenue basis: In FY2025, GoTo facilitated over Rp 600 trillion in Gross Transaction Value (GTV), but reported only Rp 18,322.2 billion in Net Revenue. Driver and merchant promotional subsidies were properly deducted from gross revenue.

slides.subtitle: One-Time Items Masking Operations: Transitory Paper Gains
slides.raw_text:
RED FLAG 2 OF 4 ,  REAL ACCOUNTING
One-Time Items Masking Operations
Restructuring Gains & Goodwill Write-Downs
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 7
slides.theory_explanation: Companies under pressure frequently use non-operating transactions to manufacture accounting profits. By recognizing one-time gains from asset disposals, litigation settlements, or deconsolidations, management masks deteriorating operating margins. Conversely, taking a 'big bath' write-down clears future balance sheets to make future earnings look artificially strong.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo experienced both extremes: In 2023, it took a massive 'big bath' goodwill impairment of -(Rp 79,481.2 bn). In 2024, it booked a paper gain of +Rp 70,300.0 bn from losing control of Tokopedia. Analysts must strip both out to reveal the true recurring operating loss.

Related-Party Concentration
Transactions with Affiliated Entities & Associates

slides.theory_explanation: Related-party transactions create significant risk of earnings management because prices and terms may not be negotiated at arm's length. A company can artificially boost revenue by charging inflated management fees to an associate, or defer expenses by transferring costs to an affiliated entity.

Inconsistent Segment Reporting
Changing Boundaries to Mask Bleeding Cash

Merging a bleeding division into a profitable one or changing revenue allocation methodologies breaks historical trend lines and obscures where capital is being destroyed.

slides.subtitle: Accruals-Based Quality Measures: The Sloan Accrual Formula
slides.raw_text:
A QUANTIFIABLE SIGNAL
Accruals-Based Quality Measures
Net Income vs. Operating Cash Flow
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 7
slides.theory_explanation: Richard Sloan (1996) demonstrated that earnings quality can be quantitatively measured using the Accrual Ratio: Accruals = Net Income - Operating Cash Flow (CFO). A high positive accrual ratio indicates that net income is driven by non-cash accounting entries (such as rising receivables or capitalized costs), signaling that earnings are low-quality and likely to reverse.
slides.goto_explanation: For GoTo FY2025: Net Income = -(Rp 1,501.7 bn), CFO = +Rp 307.0 bn. Accruals = -(1,501.7) - 307.0 = -(Rp 1,808.7 bn). Dividing by Average Total Assets (Rp 45,952.3 bn) yields a Sloan Accrual Ratio of -3.94%.

slides.subtitle: High Accruals, Lower Quality: Empirical Evidence from Sloan & Dechow
slides.raw_text:
THE RESEARCH BEHIND IT
High Accruals, Lower Quality
The Sloan Accrual Anomaly
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 7
slides.theory_explanation: Extensive academic literature (Sloan 1996; Dechow & Dichev 2002) establishes that cash flows are far more persistent than accruals. Companies in the highest decile of accruals experience subsequent earnings declines and stock underperformance, while companies with low or negative accruals experience earnings persistence and upward revisions.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo's transition from massive negative accruals in 2023 (distorted by goodwill write-downs) to a clean -3.94% accrual ratio in 2025 demonstrates that GoTo's earnings quality has normalized. Its reported numbers now accurately reflect real underlying cash dynamics.

slides.subtitle: Enron & WorldCom: The Global Precedents for Modern Accounting Traps

BRIEF INTERNATIONAL CONTEXT
Enron & WorldCom
Mark-to-Market SPVs & Capitalizing Operating Expenses
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 7
slides.theory_explanation: Two global scandals define modern forensic accounting: (1) Enron (2001) used Special Purpose Entities (SPEs) and mark-to-market accounting on long-term contracts to hide debt and invent paper profits. (2) WorldCom (2002) committed a $11 billion fraud by capitalizing regular operating telecommunication 'line costs' into capital expenditures (PP&E), turning a massive operating loss into a fake profit.
slides.goto_explanation: WorldCom is the crucial warning case for GoTo: WorldCom classified normal operating expenses as Capex to inflate EBITDA and Operating Income. GoTo capitalized Rp 880.3 billion of software development in FY2025. While fully legal under PSAK 19, analysts must verify that these capitalized costs represent genuine future economic assets rather than deferred operating maintenance.

slides.subtitle: Lessons Across All Cases: The 5 Golden Rules of Forensic Accounting
slides.raw_text:

Lessons Across All Four Cases
The Five Golden Rules of Forensic Financial Analysis
Financial Statement Analysis • Week 7

Analyzing Financing Activities
Debt vs. Equity • Bonds & Leases • Off-Balance-Sheet • Hybrid Securities • Ratio Effects
Week 9 ,  Readings: Wahlen, Baginski & Bradshaw Ch. 7 • Subramanyam Ch. 3
slides.theory_explanation: Financing activities govern how an enterprise funds its operating assets and strategic growth. Corporate finance evaluates the fundamental trade-off between debt (lower required return due to tax deductibility and contractual seniority, but rigid bankruptcy risk) and equity (higher required return and dilution, but permanent capital with zero default risk). Analysts must dissect the entire liability structure: short-term borrowings, bank debt, capitalized lease obligations under PSAK 73, and hybrid securities.
slides.goto_explanation: For PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, FY2025 marked a pivotal capital restructuring. Total interest-bearing debt surged +102.7% YoY from Rp 3,820.0 billion to Rp 7,742.6 billion, driven by new syndicated bank facilities (UOB & DBS) and USD 185M equity-linked convertible bonds (IFC & WAF). Meanwhile, GoTo capitalized Rp 155.6 billion of lease liabilities under PSAK 73 and maintained Rp 21.8 trillion in liquid cash to backstop refinancing obligations.

slides.header: A Real Number: GoTo's Cost of Debt & Interest Rate Spectrum
slides.subtitle: Why Borrowing Costs Vary Across Lenders, Facilities & Currencies
slides.raw_text:

ABBA 's Real Cost of Debt
ONE COMPANY, ONE BALANCE SHEET DATE: 0% to 12%
Why would the SAME company pay wildly different rates to different lenders?
slides.theory_explanation: A company does not have a single cost of debt; it negotiates a spectrum of borrowing rates across different credit facilities. Differences in lending rates reflect four economic drivers: (1) credit risk of the borrowing entity, (2) seniority and collateral pledged, (3) loan maturity tenure, and (4) currency denomination and inflation expectations.

Framework to Consider: Credit Risk • Collateral & Seniority • Currency • Maturity
Factor: How it moves the rate. A riskier borrower pays more; secured debt is cheaper.
slides.theory_explanation: Lenders price debt based on risk-adjusted expected recovery. Senior secured debt claims specific identifiable assets or revenue streams, granting legal priority in default and lowering the borrowing margin. Conversely, unsecured debt demands higher risk premiums. Foreign currency debt introduces exchange rate risk: if the domestic operating currency depreciates, debt service burdens expand automatically.

slides.header: The Fundamental Tradeoff: Debt vs. Equity in GoTo's Capital Stack
slides.subtitle: Balancing Tax Shield & Leverage vs. Bankruptcy Risk & Retained Deficits
slides.raw_text:
T H E  F U N D A M E N T A L  T R A D E O F F
Debt vs. Equity
DEBT: Cheaper (tax-deductible), no dilution, fixed obligation, repaid first in liquidation.
EQUITY: More expensive, dilutes ownership, no obligation to pay dividends, residual claim.
slides.theory_explanation: Modigliani-Miller theorem with taxes demonstrates that debt financing provides valuable corporate tax shields because interest payments are tax-deductible. However, increasing debt raises the probability of financial distress and agency costs. Equity offers permanent loss-absorption capacity without insolvency risk, but dilutes existing shareholders and requires higher returns.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo's capital structure is uniquely constrained by its accumulated deficit of -(Rp 215.3 trillion). Because GoTo generates pre-tax operating losses, the interest tax shield (Rp 535.2 bn interest x 22% tax rate = Rp 117.7 bn) cannot be monetized immediately, remaining deferred tax assets with full valuation allowance. Equity remains GoTo primary loss absorber.

slides.header: Instrument 1 of 3: Bond Accounting & Effective Interest Amortization
slides.subtitle: Face Value, Stated Coupon, Market Rate & Net Carrying Value
slides.raw_text:
I N S T R U M E N T  1  O F  3
Bonds: Key Features
Face Value: amount repaid at maturity • Coupon Rate: stated rate setting periodic cash interest
Market Rate: what investors actually require ,  may differ from coupon.
slides.theory_explanation: Bonds are formal debt contracts where the issuer promises periodic coupon payments and face value repayment at maturity. Under PSAK 71 / IFRS 9, bonds are initially recognized at fair value net of directly attributable transaction costs. The discount or premium is amortized over the bond tenure using the Effective Interest Method, aligning interest expense with economic borrowing costs.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo applies the effective interest method to its borrowings and equity-linked notes. When issuing USD 150M notes to IFC in October 2023, GoTo incurred Rp 57.0 billion in debt issuance costs. These costs were deducted from the initial carrying value and are steadily amortized into finance costs over the bond term, rather than expensed immediately.

slides.header: How Bonds are Priced: Discount, Par, Premium & Yield Dynamics
slides.subtitle: Connecting Present Value of Cash Flows to Balance Sheet Carrying Values
slides.raw_text:
H O W  B O N D S  A R E  P R I C E D
Discount, Par, or Premium
Coupon < Market Rate -> DISCOUNT • Coupon = Market Rate -> PAR • Coupon > Market Rate -> PREMIUM
Bond price is the present value of coupon annuity plus present value of face value.
slides.theory_explanation: Bond pricing is the mathematical present value of future cash flows discounted at the prevailing market interest rate. When the contractual coupon is below market yield, investors pay less than par value (Discount). When coupon exceeds yield, the bond sells at a Premium. Over time, amortizing the discount or premium pulls the carrying value toward par at maturity.
slides.goto_explanation: In GoTo's context, corporate borrowing facilities and hybrid bonds are issued under dynamic market interest rate environments. For example, rising global SOFR benchmark rates increased the effective yield required on USD debt, expanding GoTo's annual finance costs from Rp 245.8 billion in 2024 to Rp 535.2 billion in 2025.

slides.header: Instrument 2 of 3: Leases - Evolution to PSAK 73 / IFRS 16
slides.subtitle: How Lease Capitalization Transformed Operating Leases into Financial Debt
slides.raw_text:
I N S T R U M E N T  2  O F  3
Leases: The Historical Distinction
Finance / Capital Lease: Asset and liability appear on balance sheet.
Operating Lease: Off-balance-sheet rental expense only. (This was the rule before 2019).
PSAK 73 / IFRS 16 ended this loophole.
slides.theory_explanation: Historically, companies structured long-term lease agreements as 'operating leases' to keep billions in financial commitments off the balance sheet, artificially flattering leverage ratios. PSAK 73 (effective 2020 in Indonesia, mirroring IFRS 16) eliminated this loophole by requiring lessees to capitalize virtually all leases, recognizing a Right-of-Use (ROU) asset and a corresponding lease liability.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo complies fully with PSAK 73. All long-term property, office, and server leases are capitalized on the balance sheet. In FY2025, GoTo reported Rp 155.6 billion in total lease liabilities. The accounting shift eliminated rental opex from operating expenses, replacing it with ROU depreciation and finance charges, which artificially enhances GoTo's reported adjusted EBITDA.

Analysts must audit future minimum lease commitments.

What Remains Off-Balance-Sheet Today
Short-term and low-value leases exempt under PSAK 73 • Guarantees and contingent liabilities • Commitments.

slides.header: Instrument 3 of 3: Hybrid Securities & Embedded Equity Options
slides.subtitle: Convertible Debt, Bifurcated Equity Components & PSAK 71 Accounting
slides.raw_text:
I N S T R U M E N T  3  O F  3
Hybrid Securities
An instrument that blends debt and equity characteristics.
A convertible bond pays interest like debt ,  but gives the holder the right to convert into equity.
slides.theory_explanation: Hybrid securities bridge the gap between traditional fixed-income debt and common equity. Convertible bonds give holders regular coupon interest with downside protection, plus an embedded call option to convert into shares if stock prices rise. Under PSAK 71 / PSAK 50 (IAS 32), issuers must split the proceeds into a financial liability host and an equity conversion component.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo financing includes significant hybrid securities: USD 185M in equity-linked convertible bonds issued to the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and WAF Investments. In GoTo's balance sheet, these are recognized under non-bank borrowings (Note 20c), with the equity conversion feature offering upside while preserving cash through lower nominal interest rates.

Analysts must model both outcomes: repayment vs. conversion.
slides.theory_explanation: When analyzing convertible securities, analysts must model two distinct scenarios: (1) Repayment Scenario: If the share price stays below the conversion price, the bond acts as pure debt, requiring cash refinancing at maturity. slides.header: Bringing It Together: How Financing Choices Drive Financial Ratios
slides.subtitle: Quantifying the Impact of Debt Gearing on DuPont ROE, Solvency & Coverage
slides.raw_text:
B R I N G I N G  I T  T O G E T H E R
How Financing Choices Move Ratios
Debt-to-Assets / Debt-to-Equity: Both rise directly • Equity Multiplier: Rises ,  can inflate ROE with no operating gain • Interest Coverage: Falls.
slides.theory_explanation: Financing decisions mechanically alter every key financial ratio: (1) Adding debt directly increases Debt-to-Assets and Debt-to-Equity, (2) In the DuPont framework, debt expands the Equity Multiplier (Assets/Equity), which artificially magnifies ROE during profitable periods but deepens negative ROE during loss-making years, and (3) Debt service depresses Times Interest Earned and Cash DSCR.
slides.goto_explanation: In GoTo's audited figures, financing choices created significant ratio shifts: Total Debt surged +102.7% to Rp 7,742.6 billion, expanding Debt-to-Parent-Equity from 16.9% to 49.5%. The Equity Multiplier rose to 1.593x. Because GoTo remains operating loss-making, financial leverage actively magnified its negative return on equity (-5.23%).

slides.header: Key Takeaways: GoTo Financing Architecture & Five Analytical Rules
slides.subtitle: Core Principles for Modeling Debt, Leases, Hybrids & Capital Costs
slides.raw_text:
K E Y  T A K E A W A Y S
What to Remember from Today:
1. Debt is cheaper but rigid; equity is flexible but expensive • 2. Bond effective interest amortization
3. PSAK 73 lease capitalization • 4. Hybrid securities split accounting • 5. Ratio distortions.

slides.theory_explanation: Investing activities govern how an enterprise deploys capital into long-term revenue-generating assets. slides.header: Where the Money Goes: Capital Expenditure vs. Operating Expense
slides.subtitle: Cash Outflow Once vs. Multi-Year Amortization Cycles in GoTo's Software Stack
slides.raw_text:

A Machine: Cash Once, Profit for Years
Investing cash flow: cash goes out once • P&L: depreciation spreads cost across useful life.
Carrying value steadily declines over time.
slides.theory_explanation: Capital expenditure (Capex) represents cash invested today in long-lived productive assets that will yield economic benefits across multiple accounting periods. The matching principle dictates that this cash outflow is capitalized on the balance sheet and expensed systematically via depreciation and amortization over its useful life, preventing a massive single-period profit distortion.

In FY2025, GoTo spent Rp 1,182.4 billion in total Capex: Rp 880.3 billion capitalized into intangible software assets (Note 12) and Rp 302.1 billion in computer/server hardware (Note 13). This software is amortized straight-line over 3 to 4 years.

slides.header: Three Words for Today: Investment, Depreciation, and Impairment
slides.subtitle: The Decision, The Schedule, and The Periodic Valuation Verdict
slides.raw_text:
T H R E E  W O R D S  F O R  T O D A Y
Decision, Schedule, Verdict
INVESTMENT: The decision (cash goes out once).
DEPRECIATION: The schedule (cost spread over useful life).
IMPAIRMENT: The verdict (event-driven write-down if fair value collapses).
slides.theory_explanation: Investing accounting revolves around three chronological phases: (1) Investment: the initial capital allocation decision recorded at historical cost, (2) Depreciation/Amortization: the predictable scheduled allocation of cost across useful economic life, and (3) Impairment: an event-driven test required when economic triggers indicate that the asset's recoverable amount has fallen permanently below its carrying value.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo illustrates all three concepts with extreme clarity: (1) Investment: Rp 1.18T deployed into software and IT in 2025, (2) Depreciation/Amortization: scheduled Rp 718.5 bn annual non-cash expense, and (3) Impairment: the traumatic Rp 79.5T goodwill write-down in 2023 when Tokopedia e-commerce cash flows failed to justify their carrying value, followed by an additional Rp 356.8 bn fintech goodwill impairment in 2025.

slides.header: PP&E Part 1 of 2: Depreciation Methods & Useful Life Estimates
slides.subtitle: Straight-Line vs. Accelerated Depreciation Policies under PSAK 16
slides.raw_text:
P P & E ,  P A R T  1  O F  2
Depreciation Method Choices
Straight-Line: equal expense every period (moderate, level expense).
Declining Balance: higher expense early, lower later.
Units-of-Production: varies directly with machine usage.
slides.theory_explanation: Under PSAK 16, management must select a depreciation method that reflects the pattern in which the asset's economic benefits are consumed. The Straight-Line method recognizes equal expense across time, stabilizing reported operating earnings. Accelerated methods (Double Declining Balance) front-load depreciation, depressing near-term profits but providing conservative balance sheet asset values.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo uniformly applies the Straight-Line depreciation method across all tangible assets: computer and IT equipment (3 to 4 years), office furniture and fixtures (4 to 8 years), and vehicles (4 to 8 years). Residual values are assumed to be zero. This straight-line policy avoids earnings volatility and matches tech equipment obsolescence.

slides.header: PP&E Part 2 of 2: Impairment Mechanics under PSAK 48
slides.subtitle: Carrying Value vs. Recoverable Amount: Fair Value Less Disposal vs. Value in Use
slides.raw_text:
P P & E ,  P A R T  2  O F  2
Impairment: A Different Question
Has something happened that makes the asset worth substantially less ,  right now?
If Carrying Value > Recoverable Amount -> write down to Recoverable Amount.
Recoverable Amount = higher of (Fair Value less costs of disposal, Value in Use).
slides.theory_explanation: Under PSAK 48 (IAS 36), an asset is impaired when its carrying value exceeds its recoverable amount. The Recoverable Amount is defined strictly as the higher of: (1) Fair Value less costs of disposal (what the asset would fetch in an orderly sale today), and (2) Value in Use (the discounted present value of future cash flows expected to be derived from the asset's continued operation).
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo conducts formal impairment testing across its Cash-Generating Units (CGUs) whenever impairment indicators emerge. In FY2025, GoTo tested its On-Demand Services, Financial Technology, and Corporate software platforms. While On-Demand passed its impairment test due to narrowing operating losses, the Financial Technology CGU recognized an impairment charge against residual acquisition assets.

slides.header: Worked Example: Computing an Impairment Loss Step-by-Step
slides.subtitle: Valuation Math: Carrying Value vs. Value in Use vs. Fair Value
slides.raw_text:
W O R K E D  E X A M P L E
Computing an Impairment Loss
Carrying value: Rp 45m • Estimated recoverable amount: Rp 32m
Impairment loss = 45 - 32 = Rp 13m.
P&L: Impairment loss expense (reduces net income) • Balance Sheet: asset reduced to Rp 32m.
slides.theory_explanation: When calculating an impairment loss, the loss amount equals Carrying Value minus Recoverable Amount. The accounting entry debits 'Impairment Loss' in the Income Statement (operating expense) and credits 'Accumulated Impairment' on the Balance Sheet. Depreciation in future periods is recalculated based on the new reduced carrying value across the remaining useful life.

slides.header: Intangible Assets: Definite-Life vs. Indefinite-Life Accounting
slides.subtitle: Amortization of Proprietary Software vs. Annual Impairment of Goodwill
slides.raw_text:
I N T A N G I B L E  A S S E T S
Definite-Life vs. Indefinite-Life
DEFINITE-LIFE: Patents, licenses, software, customer lists -> amortized over useful life.
INDEFINITE-LIFE: Goodwill and brand trademarks -> NEVER amortized; tested annually for impairment.
slides.theory_explanation: Intangible assets fall into two distinct accounting categories under PSAK 19: (1) Definite-life intangibles have a determinable economic lifespan (e.g., software licenses, patents, development rights) and must be systematically amortized over that period. (2) Indefinite-life intangibles have no foreseeable limit to cash generation (e.g., goodwill) and are prohibited from being amortized; instead, they must be tested for impairment at least annually.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo holds Rp 1,565.1 billion in intangible assets (Note 12), consisting almost entirely of capitalized software development costs and electronic money/fintech licenses. These software assets are definite-life and amortized straight-line over 3 to 4 years. Meanwhile, GoTo's goodwill is indefinite-life, tested annually under PSAK 48.

slides.header: What Goodwill Represents: Purchase Price vs. Identifiable Net Assets
slides.subtitle: The Anatomy of GoTo's Legendary Rp 93.8 Trillion Historical Goodwill
slides.raw_text:
W H A T  G O O D W I L L  R E P R E S E N T S
Goodwill = Purchase Price - Fair Value of Identifiable Net Assets Acquired
Represents what cannot be separately identified: reputation, assembled workforce, expected synergies.
A goodwill impairment is an admission of past overpayment.
slides.theory_explanation: Goodwill arises in a business combination under PSAK 22 (IFRS 3) as the excess of the purchase price over the net fair value of identifiable assets and liabilities acquired. Goodwill cannot be amortized. When expected acquisition synergies fail to materialize, the company must write down goodwill via an impairment loss. A goodwill impairment is an irrevocable forensic admission that management overpaid for the target.
slides.goto_explanation: In 2021, Gojek merged with Tokopedia to form GoTo, creating Rp 93.8 trillion in goodwill based on projected e-commerce and ride-hailing synergies. When rising interest rates, slowing consumer demand, and intense competition from Shopee and TikTok destroyed those synergy projections, GoTo wrote off Rp 79.5 trillion in FY2023, and derecognized the rest upon deconsolidation in 2024.

Three Levels of Influence
< 20%: Passive Investment -> Fair value / cost; no influence.
20% - 50%: Significant Influence -> Equity Method (PSAK 15).
> 50%: Control -> Full Consolidation (PSAK 65).
slides.theory_explanation: Accounting for intercorporate investments is governed by the economic degree of influence: (1) Passive (<20% ownership): investor cannot participate in operating decisions; recorded at Fair Value through P&L or OCI. (2) Significant Influence (20% to 50% ownership): investor participates in policy-making through board seats; accounted for via the Equity Method. (3) Control (>50% ownership or de facto power): investor directs relevant activities; requires Full Consolidation.

slides.header: Treatment 1 of 2: Equity Method Mechanics under PSAK 15
slides.subtitle: Single-Line Accounting: Initial Cost + Share of Profit - Dividends Received
slides.raw_text:
T R E A T M E N T  1  O F  2
Equity Method Mechanics
Investment recorded at cost, then each period:
+ Share of Investee's Net Income • - Share of Dividends Received.
One line on the balance sheet. One line on the income statement. Nothing else appears.
slides.theory_explanation: Under PSAK 15 (IAS 28), the Equity Method treats the investment as a single expanding or contracting asset line: (1) Balance Sheet: Carrying value = Initial Cost + Cumulative Share of Investee Net Income - Cumulative Dividends Received - Impairments. (2) Income Statement: Investor recognizes its proportionate share of investee net profit or loss as a single line 'Share of Profit/(Loss) of Associates'.

In FY2025, Tokopedia's operational turnaround and Bank Jago's profitable loan expansion contributed positive equity pickups, expanding the carrying value from Rp 10,416.3 billion to Rp 10,594.8 billion (+Rp 178.5 billion net increase). GoTo receives zero cash dividends, so the entire increase represents undistributed book earnings.

slides.header: Treatment 2 of 2: Consolidation Mechanics & NCI under PSAK 65
slides.subtitle: 100% Line-by-Line Aggregation and the Non-Controlling Interest Deduction
slides.raw_text:
T R E A T M E N T  2  O F  2
Consolidation Mechanics
100% of the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses combined line-by-line with the parent.
A Non-Controlling Interest (NCI) line represents the portion owned by outside shareholders.
slides.theory_explanation: Under PSAK 65 (IFRS 10), when a parent controls a subsidiary, it must consolidate 100% of the subsidiary's revenues, expenses, assets, and liabilities line-by-line, regardless of whether it owns 100% or only 60%. To prevent overstating shareholder wealth, a separate line item 'Non-Controlling Interest' (NCI) is presented in equity and profit to represent the minority shareholders' economic claim.

In equity, GoTo presents a negative Non-Controlling Interest balance of -(Rp 3,093.4 billion) in FY2025 (2024: -(Rp 2,585.4 bn)), reflecting accumulated losses in partially owned fintech subsidiaries where minority partners absorb losses.

slides.header: The Answer: Two Roads to Zero for Associate Investments
slides.subtitle: Ordinary Equity-Method Loss Absorption vs. Sudden Event-Driven Impairments
slides.raw_text:
T H E  A N S W E R
Two Roads to Zero
Road 1: Ordinary equity-method loss recognition (investee keeps losing money; stops at zero).
Road 2: Event-driven impairment write-down (abrupt collapse in fair value).
Which road did the company take?
slides.theory_explanation: An investment in an associate can reach a zero carrying value via two very different paths: (1) The Slow Bleed (Ordinary Equity Losses): Under PSAK 15, the investor subtracts its share of losses each year until the carrying value hits zero. The investor stops recognizing further losses unless it has legal guarantees to fund them. (2) The Sudden Cliff (Event-Driven Impairment): Under PSAK 48, an abrupt economic shock or business failure triggers an immediate write-down to recoverable amount.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo experienced both roads: In 2023, its investment in Tokopedia suffered 'The Sudden Cliff' via a catastrophic Rp 79.5T goodwill write-down. In contrast, smaller joint ventures and early-stage tech bets (e.g., PT E-Commerce logistics ventures) walked 'The Slow Bleed', where cumulative operational losses eroded their carrying amounts down to zero, after which GoTo halted loss recognition.

slides.header: Adjustment 1 of 2: Equity Method Cautions - Invisible Associate Debt
slides.subtitle: Why Off-Balance Sheet Associate Leverage Flutters Reported Solvency Ratios
slides.raw_text:
A D J U S T M E N T  1  O F  2
Equity Method Cautions
The investee's own debt and liabilities are invisible ,  only the single net 'investment' line appears.
A carrying value near zero does not mean the investee stopped operating.
Analysts must inspect investee balance sheets.
slides.theory_explanation: The Equity Method is often referred to as 'one-line consolidation' because it compresses the investee's entire balance sheet into a single asset line. Crucially, the associate's debt, lease obligations, and operational liabilities are completely invisible on the investor's balance sheet. A company can use equity associates to keep massive debt off its balance sheet while retaining economic exposure.

If Tokopedia requires capital injections or Bank Jago faces liquidity pressures, GoTo may face capital calls despite their liabilities being off-balance sheet.

Consolidation & NCI Cautions
Ratios from consolidated totals include 100% of a subsidiary even where the parent owns less.

Exclude Non-Controlling Interest when computing ratios for common shareholders.
slides.theory_explanation: Consolidated financial statements aggregate 100% of subsidiary assets and liabilities, creating two critical analytical distortions: (1) Return on Equity (ROE) must be computed using Net Income Attributable to Parent divided by Parent Equity, not consolidated totals. (2) Gearing and Solvency ratios should be checked against Parent Equity to evaluate true claim dilution.

Under PSAK 72, the total transaction price must be allocated across obligations based on relative standalone selling prices. Revenue cannot be recognized for unfulfilled promises even if cash was collected upfront.

GoTo only recognizes its contracted platform take-rate (~Rp 20,000 net commission), remitting the balance to merchant and driver.

slides.header: Revenue Recognition Part 2 of 3: Point-in-Time vs. Over Time
slides.subtitle: Transfer of Control Criteria: Instantaneous Fulfillment vs. Continuous Benefit
slides.raw_text:
R E V E N U E  R E C O G N I T I O N ,  P A R T  2  O F  3
Point-in-Time vs. Over Time
POINT-IN-TIME: Satisfied at a single moment (delivery, publication, trip completion).
OVER TIME: Satisfied gradually as customer simultaneously receives and consumes benefits.
slides.theory_explanation: Under PSAK 72 paragraph 35, revenue is recognized over time if one of three criteria is met: (1) The customer simultaneously receives and consumes benefits as the entity performs, (2) The entity's performance creates or enhances an asset controlled by the customer, or (3) The performance creates an asset with no alternative use and an enforceable right to payment. Otherwise, revenue is recognized at a Point-in-Time.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo's business lines span both models: (1) On-Demand Services (Gojek rides, food delivery, courier) are recognized Point-in-Time upon trip/delivery drop-off, (2) GoPay payment transaction fees are recognized Point-in-Time upon gateway authorization, and (3) Merchant subscription services and software platform access are recognized Over Time across the subscription term.

slides.header: Inventory Costing: Why Method Selection Matters under PSAK 14
slides.subtitle: FIFO vs. Weighted Average Costing Assumptions and COGS Measurement
slides.raw_text:
I N V E N T O R Y  C O S T I N G
Why the Method Matters
Identical inventory, purchased at different prices over time.
The costing method decides which cost is expensed ,  with zero cash difference, purely an accounting assumption.
Under rising prices: FIFO yields lower COGS and higher ending inventory.
slides.theory_explanation: Under PSAK 14 (IAS 2), companies must allocate the cost of inventory available for sale between Cost of Goods Sold (Income Statement) and Ending Inventory (Balance Sheet). Under inflationary environments: (1) First-In, First-Out (FIFO) assumes oldest, cheapest units are sold first, resulting in lower COGS, higher reported profits, and higher asset values. (2) Weighted Average blends old and new costs, smoothing earnings volatility. LIFO is prohibited under IFRS and PSAK.
slides.goto_explanation: For digital platform enterprises like GoTo, physical inventory is immaterial: GoTo holds only Rp 14.1 billion in inventory (0.03% of assets) consisting of electronic payment terminals (EDC machines) and Gojek driver uniforms. GoTo uses the Weighted Average costing method, meaning inventory assumptions have zero distortive impact on GoTo's reported margins.

slides.header: Worked Example: Inventory Costing Math under Inflationary Prices
slides.subtitle: Step-by-Step Purchase History and Allocation between COGS and Ending Inventory
slides.raw_text:
W O R K E D  E X A M P L E
A Rising-Price Purchase History
Beginning: 100 units @ Rp 10,000 = Rp 1.0m • Purchase 1: 150 units @ Rp 12,000 = Rp 1.8m
Purchase 2: 100 units @ Rp 14,000 = Rp 1.4m. Total Available: 350 units = Rp 4.2m.
Assume 250 units are sold.
slides.theory_explanation: Consider 350 units available for sale costing Rp 4,200,000 total (average cost = Rp 12,000/unit). If 250 units are sold: (1) Under FIFO, the 250 units sold come from Beginning Inventory (100 units @ Rp 10,000) and Purchase 1 (150 units @ Rp 12,000), yielding COGS = Rp 2,800,000 and Ending Inventory = Rp 1,400,000 (100 units @ Rp 14,000). (2) Under Weighted Average, COGS = 250 units x Rp 12,000 = Rp 3,000,000, and Ending Inventory = 100 units x Rp 12,000 = Rp 1,200,000.
slides.goto_explanation: This classroom model explains how inventory costing creates 'phantom inventory profits': FIFO yields Rp 200,000 lower COGS and higher profits purely due to accounting assumptions, even though cash paid was identical. GoTo avoids this phantom profit issue because its Cost of Revenue consists of bank gateway fees, cloud server hosting, and driver incentive allocations.

slides.header: The Costing Result: Balance Sheet vs. P&L Trade-Off
slides.subtitle: Older Cheaper Costs Expensed First vs. Blended Unit Cost Assumptions
slides.raw_text:
T H E  R E S U L T
FIFO vs. Weighted Average
FIFO COGS: Rp 2,800,000 • Ending Inventory: Rp 1,400,000 (Older, cheaper costs expensed first).
WEIGHTED AVERAGE COGS: Rp 3,000,000 • Ending Inventory: Rp 1,200,000.
Purely an accounting allocation choice.
slides.theory_explanation: The inventory costing choice forces a trade-off between the Balance Sheet and the Income Statement: (1) FIFO provides an up-to-date Balance Sheet (ending inventory is valued at recent purchase prices), but distorts the Income Statement by matching outdated costs against current revenues. (2) Weighted Average provides a balanced compromise by smoothing unit costs across both statements.

slides.subtitle: Identifying Operating Cost Behavior across GoTo's Rp 18.7 Trillion Cost Base
slides.raw_text:
C O S T  S T R U C T U R E
Fixed vs. Variable Costs
VARIABLE: moves in direct proportion to activity (media buying, driver processing fees).
FIXED: stays largely constant regardless of activity (headcount, G&A, software R&D, servers).
slides.theory_explanation: Managerial accounting decomposes total operating expenses into: (1) Variable Costs: expenses that vary in direct proportion to business volume (e.g., payment gateway transaction fees, merchant partner commissions), and (2) Fixed Costs: expenses that remain constant regardless of output volume over the relevant range (e.g., corporate salaries, administrative office rent, core software development, scheduled depreciation).
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo's operating cost structure is heavily fixed: Out of Rp 18,700.4 billion in total operating costs in FY2025, approximately Rp 12,843.8 billion (68.7%) represents fixed or semi-fixed overhead (G&A Rp 6.14T, product development Rp 1.51T, corporate costs Rp 1.44T, and D&A Rp 0.72T). slides.header: The Formula: Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL) Mechanics
slides.subtitle: Quantifying Operating Profit Sensitivity to Top-Line Revenue Fluctuations
slides.raw_text:
T H E  F O R M U L A
Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL)
DOL = % Change in Operating Income / % Change in Revenue
A high fixed-cost base means profit swings by a LARGER percentage than revenue.
A double-edged sword: accelerates growth when rising; deepens losses when falling.
slides.theory_explanation: The Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL) measures the sensitivity of a company's operating income to percentage changes in revenue: $\text{DOL} = \frac{\% \Delta \text{Operating Income}}{\% \Delta \text{Revenue}} = \frac{\text{Contribution Margin}}{\text{Operating Income}}$. A DOL greater than 1.0 indicates that fixed costs magnify percentage changes in operating profit. Near the operating breakeven point, DOL approaches extreme or unstable values.
slides.goto_explanation: Between FY2024 and FY2025, GoTo demonstrated extreme operating leverage: Net Revenue rose +15.27%, while Operating Loss contracted by -83.12% (from -Rp 2,240.8 bn to -Rp 378.1 bn). This yields an implied empirical DOL of **5.44x** ($83.12\% \div 15.27\%$). Operating performance improved 5.44 times faster than top-line growth due to fixed overhead dilution.

slides.header: The Puzzle Resolved: Why Operating Losses Collapsed by 83.1%
slides.subtitle: Fixed-Cost Dilution, Incremental Flow-Through & Breakeven Sensitivity
slides.raw_text:
T H E  P U Z Z L E ,  R E S O L V E D
Why the Loss Shrank So Fast
Improving gross margin was magnified by a fixed-cost burden that refused to grow.
Implied DOL ≈ 83.12% ÷ 15.27% ≈ 5.44x.
A high-DOL cost structure works both ways.

Because fixed overhead has already been absorbed by baseline revenue, every additional rupiah of revenue contributes its full gross margin (68.0%) directly toward wiping out the remaining operating deficit. This high flow-through rate resolves the puzzle of why GoTo's loss fell 5.44x faster than revenue expanded.

At its 68.04% gross margin, this corresponds to an incremental revenue target of only **Rp 816.9 billion** (~4.4% additional growth over FY2025 revenue). GoTo is positioned directly on the threshold of sustained operating profitability.

T H E  P R A C T I C A L  S K I L L
What to Look for in Segment Notes

slides.theory_explanation: An analyst reviewing segment disclosures must execute three diagnostic tests: (1) Growth Concentration Test: Determine whether revenue expansion is company-wide or driven by a single volatile division, (2) Cross-Subsidization Test: Identify which business units generate real cash earnings vs those that drain corporate capital, and (3) Structural Comparability Test: Verify whether management changed segment definitions, merged units, or altered corporate cost allocations.

slides.theory_explanation: Forecasters constantly confront a structural anchor dilemma: should assumptions reflect a multi-year historical average (smoothing cyclical noise) or the most recent post-restructuring run-rate? slides.header: Key Classification: What Scales with Sales vs. What Doesn't
slides.subtitle: Separating Operational Working Capital from Financing & Non-Operating Accounts
slides.raw_text:
T H E  K E Y  C L A S S I F I C A T I O N
What Scales with Sales ,  and What Doesn't
SCALES WITH SALES: COGS, Receivables, Inventory, Accounts Payable.
DOES NOT SCALE DIRECTLY: Interest Expense (follows Debt), Tax (follows EBT), Debt Principal, Share Capital, Dividends.
slides.theory_explanation: A rigorous pro forma model separates accounts into two buckets: (1) Spontaneous / Operating items that scale naturally with sales (COGS, Receivables, Inventory, Payables), and (2) Discretionary / Financing items governed by contracts or capital policy (Debt held constant or scheduled, Interest = Rate x Debt, Taxes = Tax Rate x EBT, Paid-in Capital held constant).

Interest expense (Rp 788 bn in Base Case) is driven strictly by Debt x Interest Rate (10.2%).

Why Build Three Cases, Not One
A single-point forecast quietly implies false precision.
Conservative / Base / Optimistic cases bound the range of plausible futures.

Scenario analysis builds three coherent, internally consistent stories (Conservative, Base, Optimistic) to reveal asymmetric upside/downside risks, test covenant survival under stress, and establish valuation ranges.

slides.header: The Balance Sheet: The Plug Mechanic Explained
slides.subtitle: Ensuring Assets = Liabilities + Equity Every Forecast Year Without Circularity
slides.raw_text:
T H E  B A L A N C E  S H E E T
The Plug Mechanic
Most accounts forecast directly. One account must absorb whatever imbalance remains ,  conventionally, cash.
slides.theory_explanation: Because the Balance Sheet must obey Assets = Liabilities + Equity in every future period, one account must act as the balancing 'plug'. When Debt is held constant or scheduled externally, Cash & Equivalents equals Total Liabilities + Total Equity minus all Non-Cash Assets. If the Cash Flow Statement is built properly, Ending Cash on the Cash Flow Statement will equal the Balance Sheet Cash plug to the exact decimal.
slides.goto_explanation: In GoTo's Milestone 4 Pro Forma Balance Sheet, Total Debt is held constant at Rp 7,742.6 bn, and Cash acts as the balancing plug. In 2026F Base Case, Total Liabilities & Equity equal Rp 42,326 bn while Non-Cash Assets equal Rp 28,044 bn, leaving Cash = Rp 14,282 bn (a -Rp 7,473 bn cash drop confirmed by the Cash Flow Statement).

slides.header: Always Sanity-Check: Does the Cash Plug Make Economic Sense?
slides.subtitle: Diagnosing Negative Cash Plugs and Unsustainable Capital Burn
slides.raw_text:
A L W A Y S  S A N I T Y - C H E C K
Does the Plug Make Sense?
A cash plug falling toward zero or turning negative is the model's mechanical warning signal, not a spreadsheet bug.
If cash turns negative, the company MUST raise debt, issue equity, or slash Capex.
slides.theory_explanation: A negative or near-zero cash plug is the single most valuable warning signal in pro forma modeling. A business cannot operate with negative cash; therefore, a collapsing cash plug signals an impending financing deficit that forces real-world management action: raising high-cost debt, issuing dilutive equity, or cutting Capex.
slides.goto_explanation: In GoTo's Base Case, Cash drops from Rp 21.8T to Rp 968 bn by 2028F, while in the Conservative Case Cash turns deeply negative by 2027F. This sanity-check proves why management had no choice in 2024-2025 but to deconsolidate Tokopedia and cut G&A by 9.3%: continuing the 2023-2025 average burn rate is mathematically unsustainable.

slides.header: Completing the Picture: The Linked Pro Forma Cash Flow Statement
slides.subtitle: Reconciling Net Income, D&A, Working Capital & Capex to the Cash Plug
slides.raw_text:
C O M P L E T I N G  T H E  P I C T U R E
The Pro Forma Cash Flow Statement
Once the IS and BS are forecast, the CF statement follows mechanically.
Check vs Balance Sheet plug cash must equal ZERO.
slides.theory_explanation: Using the indirect method (Week 4), the Pro Forma Cash Flow Statement reconciles Pro Forma Net Income to the change in Balance Sheet Cash: CFO = Net Income + D&A - Increase in Receivables - Increase in Inventory + Increase in Payables; CFI = -Capex; CFF = Net Change in Debt - Dividends. The ultimate audit test is that Ending Cash (CF Statement) minus Cash Plug (Balance Sheet) equals exactly 0.00.

Notice that Working Capital generates slight positive cash inflows in 2027F-2028F (+Rp 11.1 bn, +Rp 12.4 bn) because GoTo's DPO (67.8 days) exceeds DSO + DIO (29.0 days), creating a negative cash conversion cycle.

slides.header: Sensitivity Analysis: Testing One Driver at a Time
slides.subtitle: Identifying Which Single Assumption Most Alters GoTo's Survival & Value
slides.raw_text:
A  S H A R P E R  Q U E S T I O N
Sensitivity Analysis
Which single assumption, if wrong, would most change the conclusion?
Test each driver one at a time, holding all others constant.
slides.theory_explanation: While scenario analysis moves multiple assumptions simultaneously, sensitivity analysis isolates ONE input variable at a time (e.g., +/- 100 bps in Opex %, +/- 200 bps in Revenue Growth, +/- 100 bps in WACC) to measure elasticity. This identifies the 'key value driver' where analytical precision matters most.
slides.goto_explanation: Running one-at-a-time sensitivity on GoTo's pro forma model proves that **Operating Expenses (% of Revenue)** is overwhelmingly the #1 value driver, followed by **Capex (% of Revenue)**. A 10% swing in DSO or DPO barely alters 2028F cash, whereas reducing Opex from 78.5% to 55.7% swings 3-year cumulative EBIT by +Rp 17.5 Trillion!

slides.header: Back to Our Hook: Resolving GoTo's Forecasting Anchor Dilemma
slides.subtitle: 3-Year Historical Average vs. Post-Restructuring Run-Rate - Why Both Matter
slides.raw_text:
B A C K  T O  O U R  H O O K
Resolving the Forecasting Dilemma
Neither anchor is simply 'wrong' ,  they answer different implicit questions.
3-year trend assumes historical industry economics reassert themselves; Run-rate assumes structural transformation holds.
slides.theory_explanation: Both forecasting anchors represent distinct economic hypotheses: (1) The 3-year historical average assumes mean reversion ,  that competitive pressures will eventually pull margins back toward multi-year averages. (2) The recent run-rate assumes a permanent structural break ,  that cost cuts and business exits have permanently reset the firm's cost curve.
slides.goto_explanation: In Milestone 4 and Assignment 14, Group 4 used the 3-year average Base Case as the conservative baseline (showing what happens if GoTo reverts to historical promo burn), while using the 2025 Run-Rate Optimistic Case as the upside bound. Presenting both answers explicitly prevents naive valuation errors.

slides.header: A Practical Resolution: Don't Average. Don't Default. Argue.
slides.subtitle: Defending Forecast Assumptions with Empirical Footnote Evidence
slides.raw_text:
A  P R A C T I C A L  R E S O L U T I O N
Don't Average. Don't Default. Argue.
Every driver must be justified with explicit evidence from strategy, segment notes, and cash flow behavior.
slides.theory_explanation: Professional financial analysts never blindly accept spreadsheet defaults or average incompatible years. Instead, they argue for each driver based on three evidence pillars: (1) Segment-level margins (is growth in high-margin or low-margin units?), (2) Structural changes (M&A or deconsolidation), and (3) Competitive dynamics.

slides.header: Handle With Care: Common Pitfalls in Pro Forma Modeling
slides.subtitle: Scaling Fixed Costs with Sales, Circular Debt Interest & Hidden Cash Burn
slides.raw_text:
H A N D L E  W I T H  C A R E
Common Pitfalls in Forecasting
1. Scaling fixed costs with revenue ,  the opposite of Week 12's DOL lesson!
2. Hidden debt or equity financing masked inside an unexamined plug.

slides.header: From Forecast to Value: Cost of Capital Is the Bridge
slides.subtitle: Matching Cash Flow Risk to the Correct Opportunity Cost of Capital
slides.raw_text:
F R O M  F O R E C A S T  T O  V A L U E
Cost of Capital Is the Bridge
The discount rate converts future forecasted cash flows or earnings into a present value today.
Match the cash flow to its capital providers: FCFF -> WACC; Net Income -> Cost of Equity.
slides.theory_explanation: Fundamental valuation enforces a strict matching rule: (1) Cash flows available to ALL capital providers (debt + equity), i.e., Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF), must be discounted at the blended Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC). (2) Cash flows or residual earnings belonging strictly to shareholders (Net Income, FCFE, Residual Income) must be discounted at the Cost of Equity (Ke).

Separately, Residual Income is discounted at Cost of Equity = 8.45% and added directly to Beginning Book Equity (Rp 28,711.7 bn) to arrive at Equity Value.

What Would You Do Instead?
Three standard workarounds when book capital structure breaks:
1. Peer average structure • 2. Target sustainable structure • 3. Market value of equity.

Where market equity is unavailable or book equity is negative, analysts use peer-average debt-to-capital ratios or management's stated long-term target leverage.

slides.header: Cost of Equity Part 1 of 2: CAPM in an Emerging Market
slides.subtitle: Adjusting Risk-Free Rate for Sovereign Default Spread and Adding Country Risk Premium
slides.raw_text:
C O S T  O F  E Q U I T Y ,  P A R T  1  O F  2
CAPM in an Emerging Market
Cost of Equity = Rf + Beta x (Mature-Market ERP + Country Risk Premium)
Remove sovereign default spread from local government yield to isolate clean Rf.
slides.theory_explanation: In an emerging market like Indonesia (rated Baa2 by Moody's), the 10-year local government bond yield (6.12%) is NOT purely risk-free; it embeds sovereign default risk. Following Damodaran's framework, analysts subtract the Baa2 sovereign default spread (1.618%) from the 10-year yield to obtain a clean Risk-Free Rate (4.502%), and then add the Baa2 Country Risk Premium (2.465%) to the Mature-Market Equity Risk Premium (4.23%).
slides.goto_explanation: Assignment 14 computes GoTo's Emerging-Market Cost of Equity using Damodaran's Jan 2026 Indonesia dataset: Rf = 6.120% - 1.618% = 4.502%. Total Equity Risk Premium = 4.23% (Mature ERP) + 2.465% (Indonesia CRP) = 6.695%. Multiplied by GoTo's Investing.com Levered Beta of 0.59, Ke = 4.502% + 0.59 x 6.695% = 8.45%.

slides.subtitle: Beta = 0.59 Yielding an 8.45% Required Return on Equity
slides.raw_text:
C O S T  O F  E Q U I T Y ,  P A R T  2  O F  2
Worked CAPM Calculation
Ke = Rf + Beta x (Mature ERP + CRP)
GoTo: 4.502% + 0.59 x (4.230% + 2.465%) = 8.45%.
slides.theory_explanation: Beta measures a stock's systematic sensitivity to overall market movements. A beta below 1.0 indicates lower systematic volatility relative to the broad index, whereas a beta above 1.0 indicates higher cyclical sensitivity. Multiplying Beta by the total Emerging-Market ERP and adding Rf yields the exact required return on equity (Ke).
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo's Investing.com Levered Beta is 0.59, reflecting lower correlation with traditional Indonesian commodity/banking index heavyweights during its Rp 50 price-floor era. Plugging Beta = 0.59 into EM CAPM yields Ke = 8.45%. (Analysts should note that if Beta rises toward 1.0 post-floor removal, Ke rises toward ~11.2%).

slides.header: Cost of Debt: The After-Tax Interest Rate Adjustment
slides.subtitle: Computing GoTo's Effective Pre-Tax (6.91%) and After-Tax (5.39%) Cost of Debt
slides.raw_text:
C O S T  O F  D E B T
The After-Tax Adjustment
After-Tax Cost of Debt = Pre-Tax Rate x (1 - Tax Rate)
GoTo: 6.91% Pre-tax rate -> 5.39% After-tax (22% Indonesian corporate tax rate).
slides.theory_explanation: Because corporate interest expense is tax-deductible, the effective economic cost of debt is lower than the stated coupon or bank interest rate by the corporate tax rate: After-Tax Rd = Pre-Tax Rd x (1 - T). Analysts compute Pre-Tax Rd either from current corporate bond yields or by dividing actual interest expense by total interest-bearing debt.

slides.header: Putting It Together: Computing GoTo's Blended WACC (7.76%)
slides.subtitle: Weighting Cost of Equity (8.45%) and After-Tax Cost of Debt (5.39%)
slides.raw_text:
P U T T I N G  I T  T O G E T H E R
WACC
WACC = (Weight of Equity x Cost of Equity) + (Weight of Debt x After-Tax Cost of Debt)
GoTo: (77.4% x 8.45%) + (22.6% x 5.39%) = 7.76%.
slides.theory_explanation: The Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) represents the minimum required return an enterprise must earn on its total invested assets to satisfy both lenders and equity shareholders. It weights the Cost of Equity and After-Tax Cost of Debt by their respective shares of total market enterprise capital (Market Value of Equity + Market/Book Value of Debt).

Every forecast cash flow in GoTo's DCF model is discounted back to present value at 7.76%.

slides.header: Valuation Method 1 of 3: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF - FCFF)
slides.subtitle: Computing Free Cash Flow to Firm, Enterprise Value & Net-Cash Equity Bridge
slides.raw_text:
V A L U A T I O N  M E T H O D  1  O F  3
Discounted Cash Flow (DCF)
FCFF = EBIAT (NOPAT) + D&A - Capex - Increase in NWC.
Enterprise Value = PV(FCFF Years 1-3) + PV(Terminal Value).
Equity Value = Enterprise Value - Net Debt.
slides.theory_explanation: The DCF model values an enterprise as the present value of all future Free Cash Flows to the Firm (FCFF) discounted at WACC. Crucially, when EBIT is negative, **Tax on EBIT must be zero** (governments do not pay cash tax refunds on losses). Finally, subtracting Net Debt (Total Debt - Cash) converts Enterprise Value into Equity Value.

Under Milestone 4 Base Case, GoTo's FCFF is -(Rp 7,738.7 bn) in 2026F, -(Rp 7,006.3 bn) in 2027F, and -(Rp 7,152.6 bn) in 2028F. Discounted at 7.76% WACC, Enterprise Value is -(Rp 142,597.7 bn). Adding GoTo's +Rp 14,012.5 bn Net Cash yields Equity Value of -(Rp 128,585.2 bn), or **-(Rp 121.1)/share**.

slides.header: The Hardest Part: Terminal Value & Gordon Growth Model
slides.subtitle: Why Fundamental g = Reinvestment x ROIC Fails for Loss-Making Firms
slides.raw_text:
T H E  H A R D E S T  P A R T
Terminal Value: Gordon Growth Model
TV = FCFF (final year) x (1 + g) / (WACC - g)
g should never exceed long-run nominal GDP growth or WACC.
slides.theory_explanation: Because Terminal Value typically drives 70% to 90% of a DCF valuation, the terminal growth rate (g) must obey two iron laws: (1) g < WACC (otherwise the denominator turns zero or negative), and (2) g <= long-run nominal GDP growth (capped at ~Rf 4.50%). Fundamental growth g = Reinvestment Rate x ROIC becomes 'not meaningful' (n.m.) when NOPAT is negative.

The workbook automatically falls back to Analyst Judgement g = 3.00% (safely below WACC 7.76%, Ke 8.45%, and the 4.50% nominal growth cap). At g = 3.0%, PV of Terminal Value represents 86.7% of Enterprise Value.

slides.header: Valuation Method 2 of 3: Residual Income (Economic Profit)
slides.subtitle: Book Equity + Present Value of Earnings Above the 8.45% Cost of Equity
slides.raw_text:
V A L U A T I O N  M E T H O D  2  O F  3
Residual Income (Economic Profit)
Residual Income = Net Income - (Beginning Book Value of Equity x Cost of Equity)
A company creates value only if it earns more than its equity cost of capital.
slides.theory_explanation: Residual Income (Edwards-Bell-Ohlson) measures true economic profit: Accounting Net Income minus a charge for the opportunity cost of shareholders' equity (Beginning Book Equity x Ke). Equity Value equals Current Book Value of Equity plus the Present Value of all future Residual Income. If a firm earns less than Ke, it trades below Book Value.
slides.goto_explanation: GoTo begins with Rp 28,711.7 bn of Book Equity (Rp 27.03/share). At Ke = 8.45%, shareholders demand +Rp 2,426.7 bn of profit in 2026F just to break even economically. Because Milestone 4 Base Case forecasts Net Losses of -(Rp 3,737.0 bn) to -(Rp 4,488.9 bn), Residual Income is -(Rp 6,163.7 bn) to -(Rp 6,253.9 bn) per year, erasing all book value and yielding **-(Rp 75.1)/share**.

slides.raw_text:
W O R K E D  E X A M P L E
Residual Income, Step by Step
BVE(t) = BVE(t-1) + Net Income - Dividends.
Equity Value = Current BVE + PV(RI 1-3) + PV(Terminal RI).
slides.theory_explanation: Clean Surplus Accounting tracks Book Equity forward year by year: Ending BVE = Beginning BVE + Net Income - Dividends. As losses shrink Book Equity, the subsequent year's Equity Charge declines slightly, yet negative Net Income keeps Residual Income deeply negative. Discounting all future Residual Income at Ke (8.45%) and adding Beginning BVE yields Equity Value.
slides.goto_explanation: In GoTo's Assignment 14 Residual Income sheet: Current BVE = +Rp 28,711.7 bn. The 3-year PV of Residual Income = -(Rp 15,860.4 bn), and the PV of Terminal Residual Income (g = 3.0%, Ke = 8.45%) = -(Rp 92,621.5 bn). Summing them gives Equity Value = -(Rp 79,770.2 bn), or **-(Rp 75.11)/share**.

slides.header: A Genuinely Good Sign: DCF and Residual Income Convergence
slides.subtitle: Why Mathematical Equivalence Holds When Accounting Is Clean
slides.raw_text:
A  G E N U I N E L Y  G O O D  S I G N
DCF and Residual Income Converge
Both models value the exact same underlying firm ,  one via cash flows, one via book equity plus economic profit.
Why do they differ slightly in finite 3-year projections?
slides.theory_explanation: In theory, DCF and Residual Income are mathematically identical when Clean Surplus Accounting holds and terminal values are consistent. In finite 3-year models, minor differences arise because DCF discounts FCFF at WACC (including Capex timing) while Residual Income discounts Net Income minus Equity Charge at Ke (anchored on Book Equity).

Residual Income is less negative (-75.1 vs -121.1) because it anchors on Rp 28.7T existing Book Equity and doesn't penalize Capex cash outlays immediately.

slides.header: Valuation Method 3 of 3: Market Multiples (Relative Valuation)
slides.subtitle: Pricing GoTo Against Pure-Play SEA Tech Peers (BUKA, GRAB, SE, BELI)
slides.raw_text:
V A L U A T I O N  M E T H O D  3  O F  3
Market Multiples
Relative valuation, not intrinsic ,  pricing your company as the market prices comparable peers.
Always match peers by industry, exclude non-comparable firms, and respect negative-earnings rules.
slides.theory_explanation: Market Multiples estimate value relative to comparable listed companies using P/E, Price-to-Book (P/B), and EV/EBITDA. Three strict rules apply: (1) Peers must share industry economics (never mix traditional media into tech superapps), (2) P/E is not meaningful ('n.m.') when EPS <= 0, and (3) EV/EBITDA yields Enterprise Value, requiring Net Cash addition / Net Debt subtraction to reach Equity Value.

Peer Median P/B is 2.30x and Peer Median EV/EBITDA is 13.25x.

W O R K E D  E X A M P L E
Applying Peer Multiples
Company Metric x Peer Median Multiple = Implied Value.
Watch out for negative EPS and Enterprise-to-Equity Net Cash bridges!
slides.theory_explanation: When applying peer multiples to a target company: (1) If Target EPS <= 0, P/E valuation is invalid ('-') and must be excluded, (2) Book Value per Share x Peer Median P/B gives Equity Value per share directly, and (3) EBITDA per Share x Peer Median EV/EBITDA gives Enterprise Value per share, so you MUST add Net Cash per share (or subtract Net Debt per share) to obtain Equity Value per share.

Averaging P/B and EV/EBITDA yields **Rp 39.80/share**.

slides.header: The Real Analytical Work: Reading the Valuation Gap
slides.subtitle: Explaining IDX Price Floor Abolition, Limited Liability & Base vs. Market Expectations
slides.raw_text:
T H E  R E A L  A N A L Y T I C A L  W O R K
Reading the Gap
Why do DCF/RI and Multiples diverge so sharply, and why does GoTo trade at Rp 25.00?
Explaining the economics ,  not just averaging the numbers.
slides.theory_explanation: The core value of valuation analysis lies in explaining WHY estimates diverge. Intrinsic models (DCF/RI) penalize ongoing losses and negative ROIC, whereas relative multiples (P/B) assume the target will eventually earn peer-level returns on equity. Moreover, equity has limited liability (stock cannot trade below Rp 0) and trades with option value on a potential turnaround.
slides.goto_explanation: Why GoTo trades at Rp 25.00: Historically, IDX's Rp 50 'gocap' price floor artificially pinned GoTo at Rp 50. After IDX abolished the Rp 50 floor on September 28, 2026 (lowering the minimum price to Rp 1), true price discovery cut GoTo in half to Rp 25.00 (0.9x book value). It sits above its Rp 13.20 net cash floor because limited liability caps downside at zero while pricing partial turnaround optionality.
